chunks: No affair distracts Him, time does not change Him, place does not contain Him, and the tongue does not describe Him. The number of drops of water, stars of the sky, currents of wind in the air, movement of ants on stone, and resting place of gnats in the dark night are not hidden from Him. He knows the places where leaves fall, and the secret movements of the pupils of the eyes.

key_terms.خَفِيَّ طَرْفِ الْأَحْدَاقِ: secret/subtle movements of the pupils of the eyes
key_terms.شَأْنٌ: affair or matter that could distract or occupy

ai.seo_question: What are the divine attributes of transcendence and knowledge in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this passage from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (AS) articulates the concept of divine omniscience (‘Ilm al-Ilahi) by contrasting God’s transcendence (tanzih) with His immanence in detail. The text emphasizes that while God is beyond spatial and temporal constraints, His knowledge encompasses the minutest phenomena, such as the fall of a leaf or the movement of an ant, reflecting the Shia scholarly understanding of God’s comprehensive awareness of both the apparent and the hidden. This serves as a reminder of God’s constant vigilance over creation, encouraging spiritual mindfulness (muraqabah).
